name: Should a custom spa be attached to the pool or built separately?

mainEntity.name: Should a custom spa be attached to the pool or built separately?
mainEntity.text: Should a custom spa be attached to the pool or built separately?

acceptedAnswer.text: An attached spa is usually the right choice when the homeowner wants one cohesive water feature and a design that visually connects the pool and spa. It can also simplify the overall look of the backyard and may allow the spa to share some infrastructure with the pool project. A separate spa can be better when the goal is year-round independent use, a quieter wellness zone, or a location closer to a primary suite, patio, or view corridor. Separate construction can also make sense on constrained sites where the spa needs to fit a different part of the yard. The choice should be driven by use patterns, circulation in the yard, and maintenance preferences, not only by initial price. In Los Angeles homes, aesthetics matter, but so do access and privacy. A good design should explain how the spa relates to the house, seating areas, and nighttime lighting.
acceptedAnswer.description: An attached spa works well when the goal is a unified pool design and shared equipment, while a separate spa can offer more privacy, flexibility, and independent use. The best choice depends on layout, budget, and how the backyard will be used.
